answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake before it can transact, like a cipher key that only opens doors its holder can afford to lose. Honest work is held up to a mirror of reputation: peers attest to completed tasks, and the stake is slashed when attestations contradict the record. In an ocean of cheap fake accounts, spinning up a thousand identities means locking a thousand stakes, so an attacker's cost rises linearly while influence stays capped by verified history.
